etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English pushen, poshen, posson, borrowed from Middle French pousser (Modern French pousser) from Old French poulser, from Latin pulsare (“to beat, strike”), frequentative of pellere (past participle pulsus). Doublet of pulsate and pulse (verb). Partly displaced native Old English sċūfan, whence Modern English shove.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To apply a force to (an object) such that it moves away from the person or thing applying the force.
(transitive) To continually attempt to persuade (a person) into a particular course of action.

quote.citation: December 7, 1710, Jonathan Swift, The Examiner, Number 18
quote.text: We are pushed for an answer.
Ambition […]  pushes the soul to such actions as are apt to procure honour and reputation to the actor.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To press or urge forward; to drive.

quote.citation: 1667, John Dryden, Annus Mirabilis: The Year of Wonders, 1666. […], London:  […]  Henry Herringman, […], →OCLC, stanza 133:

definitions.definition: (transitive) To continually promote (a point of view, a product for sale, etc.).

quote.citation: 1982 December 11, Frances Russell, “Economic performance buoys Pawley’s position”, in The Vancouver Sun (The Weekend Sun), Vancouver, BC, page A6:
quote.text: Earlier the premier had rejected outright suggestions, apparently being pushed by up to a third of the government’s 33-member caucus, that the government forget the deficit and launch a major public initiative to stimulate the economy.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To continually exert oneself in order to achieve a goal.

quote.citation: 2016, JoAnneh Nagler, How to be an artist without losing your mind, your shirt, or your creative compass, →ISBN, page 91:
quote.text: Don't think that if you keep pushing harder and harder, it will make you succeed faster or earn more.

definitions.definition: (informal, transitive, usually in present participle) To approach; to come close to.

quote.citation: 2023 October 7, Ajesh Patalay, quoting Jon Kung, “The Naked Chef 2.0”, in FT Weekend‎[2], HTSI, page 77:
quote.text: “I'm pushing 40 and on TikTok,” he says. “I feel old every day.”

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To tense the muscles in the abdomen in order to give birth or defecate.
(intransitive) To continue to attempt to persuade a person into a particular course of action.
To make a higher bid at an auction.
(poker) To make an all-in bet.
(chess, transitive) To move (a pawn) directly forward.
(computing) To add (a data item) to the top of a stack.

quote.citation: 1992, Michael A. Miller, The 68000 Microprocessor Family: Architecture, Programming, and Applications, page 47:
quote.text: When the microprocessor decodes the JSR opcode, it stores the operand into the TEMP register and pushes the current contents of the PC ($00 0128) onto the stack.

definitions.definition: (computing) To publish (an update, etc.) by transmitting it to other computers.

quote.citation: 2002, Lars Powers, Mike Snell, Visual Basic Programmer's Guide to the .NET Framework Class Library, page 968:
quote.text: Because this version of the Windows Installer is aware of the GAC, it has the capability to publish components into it.  […]  You can manually or programmatically push an assembly into the GAC by using the command-line tool Gacutil.exe.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) To thrust the points of the horns against; to gore.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Exodus 21:32:
quote.text: If the ox shall push a manservant or maidservant,  […]  the ox shall be stoned.

definitions.definition: To burst out of its pot, as a bud or shoot.
(snooker) To strike the cue ball in such a way that it stays in contact with the cue and object ball at the same time (a foul shot).
A short, directed application of force; an act of pushing.
An act of tensing the muscles of the abdomen in order to expel its contents.
A great effort (to do something).

quote.citation: 2022 February 9, E. Parpart, N. Patanasophon, “Activists push for new ammendment that would give marital rights for all”, in Thai Enquirer‎[3], retrieved 2022-02-09:
quote.text: The push to amend the Civil and Commercial Code on marriage is expected to enter parliament on Wednesday. The amendment would allow same-sex marriage  […]

definitions.definition: An attempt to persuade someone into a particular course of action.
(figurative) A force that impels or pressures one to act.

quote.citation: 1984 April 7, “Mousie Mousie Wildflower (personal advertisement)”, in Gay Community News, page 14:
quote.text: I guess it's justthe special curseof working underdeadline's push

definitions.definition: (military) A marching or drill maneuver/manoeuvre performed by moving a formation (especially a company front) forward or toward the audience, usually to accompany a dramatic climax or crescendo in the music.
A wager that results in no loss or gain for the bettor as a result of a tie or even score
(computing) The addition of a data item to the top of a stack.
(Internet, uncountable) The situation where a server sends data to a client without waiting for a request.
(slang, UK, obsolete, now chiefly Australia) A particular crowd or throng or people.

quote.citation: 1891, Banjo Paterson, An Evening in Dandaloo:
quote.text: Till some wild, excited personGalloped down the township cursing,"Sydney push have mobbed Macpherson,Roll up, Dandaloo!"

quote.citation: 1994, David Malouf, A First Place, Vintage, published 2015, page 37:
quote.text: My father  […]  was soon as unambiguously Australian as any other member of the rough Rugby pushes that in the years before the Great War made up the mixed and liverly world of South Brisbane.

definitions.definition: (snooker) A foul shot in which the cue ball is in contact with the cue and the object ball at the same time
(professional wrestling slang) An attempt to give momentum to a wrestler's career in the form of victories and/or more screen time.
A push-button, such as a bell push.

quote.text: A bell circuit, fed from the train lighting battery, is connected to a push in each berth and functions in conjunction with a luminous indicator mounted over the door and in association with a cancellation push, for use by the car attendant.
